- For a new app in an empty folder, make something the user can open and use at once: by default a web app (index.html with CSS and JavaScript, no build step and no packages unless the sandbox has package access), with a clean, modern look, plus a few tests of its logic and a short README saying how to open it. If you use packages and a bundler (React with Vite; for a new app, with OpenAI's Apps SDK UI design system as the app describes), give package.json a `build` script that writes dist/index.html with relative asset paths (Vite: `base: './'`); the app runs it when you finish. When you finish, the app opens the project's index.html (or dist/index.html) in its preview panel by itself: do not tell the user to open files by hand.

{"summary": "I created the ESM package. `npm test` runs 6 tests and all of them pass.

- `package.json` sets `"type": "module"`, and its `test` script runs `node --test`. It also exports `./src/roman.js` as the package entry.
- `src/roman.js` exports `toRoman(n)`, which converts a number to Roman numerals one place value at a time, largest first. It also handles the subtractive pairs like `CM` and `IV`.
- Anything that isn't a whole number from 1 to 3999 throws a `RangeError`. That includes numbers out of range (0, 4000, Infinity), decimals like 1.5, NaN and non-number values like `'10'` or `null`.
- `test/roman.test.js` covers single symbols, subtractive pairs, longer numbers like 1994 → `MCMXCIV`, both ends of the range (1 and 3999), and the error cases.", "outputs": ["package.json", "src/roman.js", "test/roman.test.js"], "suggestions": ["Add fromRoman(str) to parse Roman numerals back to integers", "Add a round-trip test over all values 1..3999"]}
